requirement: Describe the study as a prospective, open-label, nonrandomized, unmasked, single-arm early-feasibility device study at three US centers, with one pseudophakic study eye per participant implanted with the IOPCL AMD-MAG and followed for 12 months.

evidence.text: The protocol defines a 12-month, three-site study enrolling a maximum of 10 pseudophakic subjects.
The SAP confirms a three-center unilateral implantation study that is not randomized or masked.

requirement: State the prospective operational maximum of 10 participants and 10 unilaterally treated eyes, explain that this is an early-feasibility cap rather than a hypothesis-test power calculation, and do not substitute the registry's eventual enrollment of nine.
acceptable_values: do not use actual enrollment 9 as target

evidence.text: The protocol prospectively limits enrollment and unilateral implantation to 10 subjects or eyes.
The SAP describes 10 subjects or eyes as the EFS sample-size limit without a power calculation.

requirement: Define separate effectiveness and safety analysis populations at the participant and study-eye level, explicitly resolving whether an eye with attempted but unsuccessful implantation enters each analysis and preserving a one-eye-per-participant unit of analysis.

evidence.text: The protocol defines study-eye endpoints and unilateral implantation but does not define analysis populations.
The SAP says analyses include all eyes where implantation was attempted and/or successful and later invokes an undefined safety population.

requirement: Reconcile the stated primary objective of positional stability and adherence with the separately labelled primary effectiveness endpoint of near-visual-acuity improvement, and declare which endpoint governs any study-level success conclusion.
acceptable_values: single governing success conclusion or clearly separated safety and effectiveness conclusions

evidence.text: The protocol calls stability and adherence the primary objective but separately labels the 12-month UCNVA response as the primary effectiveness endpoint.

requirement: Define the primary effectiveness endpoint as the proportion of implanted study eyes gaining at least 10 letters in uncorrected near visual acuity measured at 14 cm at the 12-month assessment versus the protocol baseline, with the planned target that at least 75% of eyes meet the responder definition.

evidence.text: The protocol states the 10-letter UCNVA responder endpoint and 75% target at 12 months.
The SAP repeats the endpoint and plans a proportion summary.

requirement: Analyze the four prespecified secondary 12-month near-vision responder endpoints separately: at least 20-letter UCNVA gain from baseline UCNVA, at least 10- and 20-letter UCNVA gains versus baseline BCNVA, and at least 10- and 20-letter BCNVA gains versus baseline BCNVA, preserving the protocol's 75% or 50% target attached to each threshold.
acceptable_values: 20-letter UCNVA gain from baseline UCNVA with 50% target
10-letter UCNVA gain versus baseline BCNVA with 75% target
20-letter UCNVA gain versus baseline BCNVA with 50% target
10-letter BCNVA gain versus baseline BCNVA with 75% target
20-letter BCNVA gain versus baseline BCNVA with 50% target

evidence.text: The protocol enumerates the secondary responder definitions, baselines and target proportions.
The SAP carries each secondary responder endpoint into planned summaries.

requirement: Keep the near-acuity conditions distinct: postoperative UCNVA and BCNVA are measured at 14 cm, while the designated baseline BCNVA comparison is measured at 30 cm with the participant's distance correction plus a +3.0 D add; derive letter change using the corresponding prespecified baseline.

evidence.text: The protocol distinguishes the near-vision distances, correction and scheduled measurements.

requirement: For every responder endpoint, specify the evaluable-eye denominator, present the responder count and proportion with an exact binomial confidence interval, and state prospectively whether the 75% and 50% values are descriptive targets or formal success thresholds; do not imply confirmatory inference from an unqualified proportion summary.

evidence.text: The protocol supplies responder thresholds and target proportions but no inferential decision rule.
The reference only says that proportions will be summarized and does not define denominators, intervals or formal success criteria.

requirement: Supplement responder proportions with the reference-plan visual-acuity displays: descriptive UCNVA values from one month onward and mutually interpretable letter-change categories spanning loss, no change within plus or minus five letters, and gains through at least 20 letters.
acceptable_values: no change within plus or minus 5 letters

evidence.text: The SAP specifies descriptive UCNVA summaries and categorical letter-change bins for primary and secondary near-vision comparisons.

requirement: Summarize preservation of best-corrected distance and near visual acuity as the number and proportion of implanted eyes losing at least two lines or 10 letters at 12 months versus preoperative baseline, and compare the observed proportions with the protocol's less-than-5% safety targets.
acceptable_values: BCDVA loss at least 2 lines or 10 letters
BCNVA loss at least 2 lines or 10 letters

evidence.text: The protocol defines the BCDVA and BCNVA preservation thresholds and safety targets.
The SAP plans observed-data counts and percentages for the two visual-acuity loss outcomes.

requirement: Analyze device delivery and positional stability at the study-eye level, separately reporting successful delivery, UBM-defined maintenance of the inter-lens gap within plus or minus 10 microns, PCIOL and IOPCL tilt no greater than 10 degrees, and IOPCL centration with exposed PCIOL area between 0.25 and 0.75 mm.
acceptable_values: UBM gap change within plus or minus 10 microns
PCIOL tilt no greater than 10 degrees
IOPCL tilt no greater than 10 degrees

evidence.text: The protocol defines successful delivery, gap, tilt and centration criteria.
The SAP plans counts and proportions for delivery, spacing, decentration and tilt.

requirement: Prespecify evaluation of the trial suspension rule triggered by either two or more consecutive severe ocular injuries or two or more participants at any one site requiring explant for visual intolerance when related to the procedure or device.
acceptable_values: two or more consecutive severe ocular injuries

evidence.text: The protocol defines the two-part safety stopping rule and site-level trigger.

requirement: Summarize intraoperative and postoperative adverse events by event type and scheduled visit and cumulatively, distinguishing participant or eye incidence from event counts, persistence, seriousness, severity, relatedness and device/procedure attribution.

evidence.text: The protocol defines adverse-event collection across operative and follow-up visits and lists ocular event categories.
The SAP requests number and percent of eyes by scheduled visit and cumulative or persistent status.

requirement: Report secondary surgical interventions by category as cumulative numbers and proportions of study eyes and provide a listing with study identifier, visit, date, category and clinical sequelae, excluding Nd:YAG treatment for posterior capsular opacification from the SSI endpoint as specified.

evidence.text: The protocol names SSI examples and excludes Nd:YAG treatment for PCO.
The SAP specifies cumulative SSI summaries and a detailed line listing.

requirement: Map nominal visits to the protocol windows: preoperative, operative, 1-2 days, 7-14 days, 30-60 days, 120-180 days and 330-420 days after implantation, and apply the separate analogous post-explantation schedule without mixing post-implant and post-removal observations.

evidence.text: The protocol lists the implantation and post-explantation visit windows.

requirement: State that the reference uses available-data analyses with no imputation, but define endpoint-specific denominators and missingness displays and add a sensitivity or conservative interpretation for missing 12-month outcomes in this very small study, especially when missingness follows explantation, intolerance or loss to follow-up.

evidence.text: The protocol defines follow-up, termination and discontinuation but not a statistical missing-data strategy.
The SAP specifies available-data analyses with no imputation, including safety outcomes.

requirement: Define intercurrent-event strategies for explantation, reimplantation or repositioning, secondary surgery, Nd:YAG treatment, treatment-related discontinuation and death, including whether post-removal observations contribute to each effectiveness and safety estimand.

evidence.text: The protocol permits removal, defines post-removal follow-up and identifies secondary procedures and discontinuation, but does not give estimand rules.

requirement: Prespecify how the positional-stability objective, primary UCNVA responder, multiple secondary responder thresholds and numerous safety and exploratory outcomes are interpreted jointly; either define a hierarchy or multiplicity control or state that all summaries are descriptive and cannot support separate confirmatory success claims.

evidence.text: The protocol contains several target proportions and two competing primary concepts without multiplicity rules.
The reference proposes separate descriptive summaries but no hierarchy or multiplicity convention.

requirement: Describe the planned interim analysis as a descriptive early-feasibility review after every enrolled participant has reached, exited before or missed the 120-180-day visit window, with separate annual regulatory safety summaries and no efficacy alpha spending or early-success claim.
acceptable_values: interim after all participants resolve 120-180-day visit

evidence.text: The SAP defines the interim timing and annual regulatory safety summaries but no inferential boundary.

requirement: Treat improved reading speed and independence from external magnifiers as exploratory outcomes restricted to the prespecified simulation-qualified eyes, using the protocol definitions and reporting the reference-plan change categories without elevating them to confirmatory claims.
acceptable_values: at least 20-letter preoperative simulated UCNVA improvement

evidence.text: The protocol defines the simulation-qualified exploratory population and the reading-speed and magnifier targets.
The SAP provides the reading-change and magnifier-use categories.

requirement: Define baseline and derived time variables consistently: preoperative measurement is the endpoint baseline unless otherwise specified, postoperative day equals assessment date minus implantation date, age is completed years at consent, months equal days divided by 30.4375 and years equal days divided by 365.25.

evidence.text: The protocol anchors assessments to preoperative and postoperative windows.
The SAP gives the age, postoperative-day and unit-conversion derivations.

requirement: Provide visit-level descriptive summaries for MRSE and change, Goldmann IOP and change, slit-lamp, gonioscopic, fundus, OCT and contrast-sensitivity findings, endothelial cell count and change, and categorical distance and near visual acuity, retaining the protocol-defined assessment schedule.

evidence.text: The protocol lists the ophthalmic assessments and their visit schedule.
The SAP specifies descriptive and categorical summaries for these ophthalmic outcomes.

requirement: Score each VFQ-25 item using the NEI VFQ-25 scoring algorithm and summarize visit-level scores and change from preoperative using the planned descriptive statistics; separately summarize operative surgical-difficulty and capsular-tissue-handling responses by count and percentage of study eyes.

evidence.text: The protocol schedules VFQ-25 and records surgical difficulty and capsular-tissue handling.
The SAP names the NEI scoring algorithm and descriptive VFQ-25 and surgical-difficulty summaries.
